title: ANGraph: A GNN-Based Performance Prediction Framework for Asynchronous Neuromorphic Hardware
problem: Significant mismatches exist between system-level simulation predictions and gate-level simulations for asynchronous neuromorphic hardware, resulting in inaccurate performance estimates during design space exploration; this slows optimization of energy-efficient edge AI accelerators.
motivation: Asynchronous neuromorphic hardware is increasingly promising for energy-efficient edge AI, but design space exploration requires fast, accurate performance prediction to bridge the sim-to-hardware gap.
method: ANGraph starts with intermediate data from system-level simulations—fast but approximate predictions of hardware behavior—and converts them into graph structures where each node represents a circuit component and edges show how components connect. It trains a Graph Neural Network (a machine-learning model that learns patterns in connected data) using over one million detailed gate-level circuit simulations, which are highly accurate but computationally expensive. The GNN learns to predict latency—how long hardware takes to complete operations—by recognizing recurring patterns in the circuit graphs. A separate ResNet model predicts power consumption, and both models generalize across different hardware sizes, manufacturing process nodes, and varying input workloads without requiring retraining.
key_novelty: Using a Graph Neural Network to predict how fast neuromorphic hardware runs, bridging the gap between fast-but-rough system-level simulations and slow-but-precise gate-level simulations while remaining accurate across different hardware designs.
contributions: GNN-based latency prediction framework achieving R-square 0.69 improvement and 76% RMSE reduction vs. state-of-the-art simulators
ResNet-based power consumption prediction with R-square 0.98 and MAPE 0.88%
Generalization across different scales, process nodes, and input traffic patterns without additional training
Benchmark dataset with over one million gate-level simulation samples for neuromorphic hardware
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific neuromorphic architectures; applicability to synchronous or hybrid neuromorphic designs not discussed.
primary_theme: GNN-based high-fidelity performance prediction for neuromorphic hardware design optimization
